column2: p377's "query language is an instrument axis" is NARROWED, not refuted.  It holds where the language has an INDEXED DEVELOPER-FORGE POPULATION (zh, ko, pt, and partly id and fr).  It does NOT hold for hi or ar: an in-language query there returns the ENGLISH answer set, because this index has no Hindi or Arabic supply neighbourhood to reach.

🔴 So the rule is NOT "run a leg in the engagement region's language".  A successor reading p377 alone would run a Hindi leg for an India engagement and get the English index back at full price.  The rule is "run a leg in a language with an indexed forge population", and this pass's measurement says hi and ar are not such languages FROM THIS INDEX.

🔴 The NEW rate is the WRONG dial for choosing a leg, and the CORRECTED figures make the case better than the draft's did.  The four NEW rates sit in a 6.7-point band (40.0 / 33.3 / 33.3 / 33.3) while the in-language fraction ranges from 0 % (hi, ar) to 33 % (id).  So the ar leg — which returned a 100 % ENGLISH answer set — and the id leg — which reached a genuinely Indonesian repository — scored the SAME 33.3 % NEW.  🔵 The two measurements are UNCORRELATED: NEW rate measures this base's sweep history, the in-language fraction measures the leg's reach, and NEW rate cannot tell a leg that reached a foreign forge from one that did not.  A successor choosing legs by NEW rate is choosing by noise.

The yield is 0 agent rows for 4 legs and 6 NEW addresses, against p377's 1 for 4 legs and 6 NEW.  Two consecutive passes put the per-row cost of an in-language supply leg between 1-in-4 and 0-in-4.  🟢 A successor should stop buying in-language SUPPLY legs by default and spend the same budget on the GRANT gap instead: the two best near-misses across both passes (aifrenz/pcu-2026 at p377, y-kanchan/AI-Teaching-Agent here) failed on grant, not on language and not on substance.
